title: One Time production correction control tower

reasons: The packet asks to complete and deploy multiple One Time surfaces.
The packet contains CRM, portal, inbox, classroom, WhatsApp, performance, tests, screenshots, and deployment requirements.
The packet uses product-quality language and requires audit-first UI handling.
likely_external_provider_blockers: WhatsApp sends require existing provider readiness and explicit send approval.
Deployment/live-smoke requires release gate and clean lane.
Screenshots are missing from the supplied paths.
ramble_router.next_exact_packet: PKT-20260712-103 identity/view-as server scope hardening, while PKT-20260712-102 waits for screenshots.

operator_intent_summary: Register and execute a production correction for One Time CRM isolation, identity truth, portal clarity, WhatsApp launcher/assistant, performance, testing, deployment, and live verification.
raw_quotes: This is an implementation task, not an audit-only task.
Create the required raw intake, requirement register, Product Quality Compiler packet, state matrix, and execution run first.
Do not stop after creating planning documents.
No internal BNA table names appear in Rabbi UI.

decisions_captured.decision: The six source screenshot files are unavailable locally; screenshot-dependent UI implementation remains blocked until they are supplied or regenerated.
GHL-like language means first-party BNA CRM pattern inspiration only.

out_of_scope: No one giant implementation change for the entire parent packet.
No email send, WhatsApp send, charge, refund, DNS change, upload, access grant, external provider write, production hard delete, or GHL/LeadConnector runtime.
No screenshot-dependent UI implementation until current-state screenshots or regenerated audit evidence exist.
No exposure of signed view-as tokens, secrets, raw private messages, or private contact data in committed evidence.
affected_surfaces: Operations One Time identity and CRM

inspection_targets: existing prompt packets and PQC fixtures
known_blockers: The worktree has unrelated dirty/untracked files; broad product source edits must wait for scoped implementation packets.
current_state.baseline_summary: The active previous run had no unblocked batch. A new run was created and the previous blocked run was marked inactive without deleting its blocker history.

expanded_phrases.finish everything: Split the parent request into source-covered requirements, child packets, verification gates, deployment gates, and terminal statuses instead of one oversized implementation.
expanded_phrases.CRM: First-party scoped contact list/detail, lifecycle, source, tags, owner, last activity, timeline, notes, tasks, membership/access, and conversation views with tenant isolation.
expanded_phrases.GHL-like: Use useful first-party CRM patterns only: list/detail, activity timeline, lifecycle, tasks, notes, inbox context, and compact filters. Do not add external CRM runtime.
expanded_phrases.portal: Family, student, classroom, library, and parent setup/reset journeys with shared One Time shell, role-appropriate links, support boundaries, and preview preservation.
expanded_phrases.working: Actions perform scoped first-party behavior or visibly show read-only/preview/blocked states with owner, reason, next action, tests, and readback.
expanded_phrases.configured: Provider/setup status is explicit, separated from normal user workflow, and does not imply external writes without approval.
expanded_phrases.launch-ready: All requirements are terminal with tests, screenshots where needed, deployment/live-smoke proof for app-visible work, and exact blockers otherwise.
expanded_phrases.professional: Consistent IA, readable contrast, compact spacing, credible CRM/portal workflows, and no debug/internal leakage.
expanded_phrases.clean: Aligned layout, readable typography, consistent states, no raw storage labels, no role leakage, and mobile/tablet/desktop proof.

product_quality_expansion.first_party_pattern_interpretation: All CRM and inbox work stays first-party BNA/One Time. No GHL, LeadConnector, external CRM writes, or external CRM UI promises are authorized.
